title: Pinchas: a covenant of peace (Numbers 25:12)
hookLine: after violent zeal, a covenant of peace, and the word "peace" is written with a broken letter

lines: THE STORY TURNS DARK AT SHITTIM.
cards: Balaam's blessings are over, and the story turns dark fast. At a place called Shittim, many Israelites are drawn into the worship of a local god, Baal of Peor. A plague breaks out in the camp.

In the middle of the crisis, a leader from the tribe of Simeon brings a Midianite woman into his tent in full view of everyone. And Pinchas, the grandson of Aaron, takes a spear, follows them in, and kills them both.
The plague stops. It's a hard scene to read. What God says next is a surprise.

teach.b: A new portion opens, named for Pinchas. God says he turned back the divine anger, and then, in the 1917 Jewish Publication Society translation: "Behold, I give unto him My covenant of peace." Peace.
To the man who just killed two people. Then a detail you can only see in a Torah scroll.

In the word shalom, peace, in this verse, the letter vav, the tall straight line in the middle, is written with a break in it. The Talmud mentions this broken vav, and Torah scribes still write it that way today.
Nobody in the text explains it, so commentators offer readings. One says the break is a warning: peace that comes after violence, even violence the text approves of, is never whole.
Something in the person who did it, or in the community, stays cracked. And the rabbis were careful about zeal in general.
The Talmud says the law permitted what Pinchas did in that exact moment, but if someone came to ask whether to do the same, they wouldn't be told yes.

One way to read it: a zealot who stops to ask has already lost the certainty the act requires. The tradition honored Pinchas and, almost in the same breath, refused to make him a model anyone should copy.
There's a Hebrew word for passionate zeal, kin'ah, and the portion uses it of Pinchas. But the reward God gives him isn't more zeal. It's peace.
As if to say: your fire stopped a plague; now carry the opposite of fire.

how: In Torah scrolls the vav of shalom in Numbers 25:12 is written with a small break, and when the portion of Pinchas is read in summer, the broken letter is often pointed out and discussed.

o: Aaron's grandson, given a covenant of peace
the local god the people worshiped at Peor
the tribal leader from Simeon who defied the camp

games.q: what's inside the verse — tap the pairs.
p: a gap in the word shalom

s: the broken vav in shalom is a printing mistake
the Talmud mentions it, and scribes still write it broken in Torah scrolls.

games.q: Pinchas has acted with violent zeal, and the plague has stopped. what does God give him?
o: the right to judge the people.
games.why: a covenant of peace. and in the scroll, the word peace is written with a broken letter.

practice: Think of something you feel so fiercely about that you've been sharp with someone over it: a cause, a value, a family rule.
Picture that broken letter, a tall line with a small gap in it, and ask where a little peace could go into the fire: a softer tone, a question instead of a verdict, an apology for how you said it.

wordCard.voice: Pinchas. The zealous grandson of Aaron, given a covenant of peace, with peace written in the scroll with a broken letter.

orig.note: Hebrew: my covenant of peace (Numbers 25:12); in Torah scrolls the vav of shalom here is written broken.

carryVoice: Your line: peace is written broken. Even the reward for zeal was peace. See you tomorrow.
